question: On 28 February 2022, Ukraine applied for European Union membership. The European Council granted candidate country status to Ukraine on 23 June 2022, and opened formal accession negotiations on 15 December 2023. The Russian Federation launched a military invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022. To date, it occupies some 18 % of Ukranian territory and maintains an active front line of a thousand kilometres. In view of this: 1.
Is the Council of the opinion that a country at war and under partial occupation, as Ukraine is, satisfies the stability criteria set in the conclusions of the1993 European Council?

Is the Council therefore of the opinion that Ukraine could join the European Union even while the war of aggression against it continues, or, on the contrary, that peace is a prerequisite to its accession?

If the former is true, and in light of Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union, what legal and practical consequences does the Council consider the accession of a country in a state of defensive war would have for other Member States, including as regards the possible obligation to join the war at Ukraine’s side?
answer: The Council has not discussed the issues raised by the Honourable Members and thus it is not in a position to reply to the second and third questions. In relation to the first question, Article 49 of the Treaty on European Union stipulates that any European State which respects the values referred to in its Article 2 and is committed to promoting them may apply to become a member of the Union.

Following the Council’s request, the Commission delivered an Opinion on Ukraine’s EU membership application on 17 June 2022 in which it assessed the application under the Copenhagen criteria, stating that ‘The resilience of Ukrainian institutions has been on full display since the Russian invasion, with the government continuing to function at all levels.

Overall, as regards the political criteria, Ukraine is well advanced in reaching the stability of institutions guaranteeing democracy, the rule of law, human rights and respect for and protection of minorities.’ The Commission recommended that Ukraine be granted candidate status.

In the light of the Commission’s Opinion, in its conclusions of 23-24 June 2022, the European Council decided to grant Ukraine the status of candidate country to Ukraine. Based on progress made by the country, on 14-15 December 2023, the European Council decided to open accession negotiations with Ukraine.
It also invited the Council to adopt the negotiating framework once the relevant steps set out in the Commission recommendation on Ukraine of 8 November 2023 are taken.

Finally, in its conclusions of 21-22 March 2024, the European Council welcomed the progress of Ukraine in advancing on the necessary reforms on their EU path and invited the Council to swiftly adopt the negotiating framework and to take work forward without delay.
